To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the cytostatic therapy for meningiomas should be based on the alkylating agent HU, which is effective at concentrations that are well tolerated by patients.

HU is the only cytotoxic drug that has a significant impact on meningioma cell growth in vitro, that the impact is moderate, and that NF2-deficient meningioma cells are more sensitive to HU than NF2-intact meningioma cells.
HU is a potential chemotherapeutic drug for meningiomas, that NF2 is a key factor for the chemosensitivity, and that other chemotherapeutic or targetted therapies are still to be evaluated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new therapeutic strategies for meningiomas.
the development of novel therapies for meningioma patients.
a better understanding of the molecular mechanisms of meningioma development.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HU is a promising candidate for further clinical studies in meningioma therapy.
HU may be considered for meningiomas, whereas all other drugs discussed in this study should be evaluated in further clinical trials.
the use of HU as the only drug for meningioma treatment is still justified.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HU remains the only drug which has a reasonable chance to be used in meningioma patients, although the clinical benefit of this drug is still to be proven.

the current knowledge of the molecular biology of meningioma and of the molecular mechanisms of the discussed chemotherapics and targeted therapies does not justify a broad use of these drugs in the clinical setting at this point of time.

the current knowledge about meningiomas and the available data from clinical studies and in vitro studies do not allow for a recommendation of any chemotherapeutic or chemopreventive treatment for meningiomas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HU may still be considered as a chemotherapeutic option for meningiomas, but the efficacy may vary considerably among patients and meningioma subtypes.
meningioma cell cultures are an excellent model for preclinical evaluation of novel therapies.
the NF2 status of meningioma cells has to be considered when assessing their response to cytostatic therapies.
